question.text: What may you do at a white painted curb?

answer.text: At a white painted curb you may stop only for as long as it takes to pick up or drop off passengers.

teaching.text: A white painted curb lets you stop only as long as it takes to pick up or drop off passengers. Remember: white: pick up, drop off.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a white painted curb you may stop only for as long as it takes to pick up or drop off passengers.

question.text: What may you do at a yellow painted curb, and what must you do while there?

answer.text: At a yellow painted curb you may stop only long enough to load or unload, and you must stay with your car.

teaching.text: A yellow painted curb lets you stop only long enough to load or unload, and you must stay with your car. Remember: yellow: load, stay with car.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a yellow painted curb you may stop only long enough to load or unload, and you must stay with your car.

question.text: What does a red painted curb mean?

answer.text: A red painted curb means you may not stop, stand or park there at all.

teaching.text: A red painted curb means no stopping, standing or parking there at any time. Remember: red: no stopping at all.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A red painted curb means you may not stop, stand or park there at all.

question.text: How do the white, yellow and red curb rules differ?

answer.text: A white curb allows a brief stop for passengers, a yellow curb allows a brief stop for loading while you stay with the car, and a red curb allows no stop at all.

teaching.text: White curbs allow a short passenger stop, yellow curbs a short loading stop while you stay with the car, and red curbs no stop at all. Remember: passengers, loading, nothing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A white curb allows a brief stop for passengers, a yellow curb allows a brief stop for loading while you stay with the car, and a red curb allows no stop at all.

question.text: Which lane is usually best when you will stay on a one-way street for several blocks?

answer.text: When you will stay on a one-way street for several blocks, the center lane is usually the best lane to use.

teaching.text: If you will stay on a one-way street for several blocks, the center lane is usually the best one to use. Remember: usually the center lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When you will stay on a one-way street for several blocks, the center lane is usually the best lane to use.

question.text: What are the left and right lanes of a one-way street used for?

answer.text: On a one-way street, the left and right lanes are used by vehicles that are turning.

teaching.text: On a one-way street, vehicles that are turning use the left and right lanes. Remember: outer lanes for turning.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a one-way street, the left and right lanes are used by vehicles that are turning.

question.text: Why is the center lane preferred on a long one-way street?

answer.text: On a long one-way street the center lane is preferred because the outer lanes serve turning vehicles.

teaching.text: On a long one-way street the center lane is preferred, because the outer lanes serve turning vehicles. Remember: outer lanes turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a long one-way street the center lane is preferred because the outer lanes serve turning vehicles.

question.text: What do white lane lines divide?

answer.text: White lane lines divide lanes of traffic heading the same way.

teaching.text: White lane lines separate lanes of traffic that are moving in the same direction. Remember: white: same direction.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: White lane lines divide lanes of traffic heading the same way.

question.text: What else may a single white line mark?

answer.text: A single white line may also mark the right edge of the pavement.

teaching.text: A single white line can also mark where the pavement ends on the right side. Remember: right pavement edge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A single white line may also mark the right edge of the pavement.

question.text: When may you cross a broken white line to change lanes?

answer.text: After you signal, you may cross a broken white line to change lanes if it is safe.

teaching.text: Once you have signaled, you may cross a broken white line to change lanes when it is safe. Remember: signal, then if safe.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After you signal, you may cross a broken white line to change lanes if it is safe.

question.text: What does a solid white line mark?

answer.text: A solid white line marks the right edge of the roadway and also divides lanes of traffic heading the same way.

teaching.text: A solid white line marks the right edge of the roadway and also separates same-direction lanes. Remember: right edge and lanes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A solid white line marks the right edge of the roadway and also divides lanes of traffic heading the same way.

question.text: When may you cross the solid white edge line on the right side of the road?

answer.text: Cross the solid white edge line on the right side of the road only in an emergency or to avoid a road hazard.

teaching.text: Only cross the solid white edge line on the right for an emergency or to avoid a hazard in the road. Remember: emergencies or hazards only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Cross the solid white edge line on the right side of the road only in an emergency or to avoid a road hazard.

question.text: When may drivers cross a solid white line beside an HOV lane?

answer.text: Drivers may cross a solid white line while merging into or out of a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane.

teaching.text: You may cross a solid white line when merging into or out of a high occupancy vehicle lane. Remember: merging in or out.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers may cross a solid white line while merging into or out of a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane.

question.text: May you cross a double solid white line?

answer.text: A double solid white line divides two lanes heading the same way, and crossing it is prohibited.

teaching.text: A double solid white line separates two same-direction lanes, and you may not cross it. Remember: double white, never cross.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A double solid white line divides two lanes heading the same way, and crossing it is prohibited.

question.text: How does a broken white line differ from a double solid white line?

answer.text: A broken white line may be crossed after signaling when safe, while a double solid white line may not be crossed.

teaching.text: A broken white line may be crossed after signaling when safe, but a double solid white line may not be crossed. Remember: broken may, double never.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A broken white line may be crossed after signaling when safe, while a double solid white line may not be crossed.

question.text: How does the right-edge solid white line differ from the line beside an HOV lane?

answer.text: The solid white right-edge line is crossed only for an emergency or a road hazard, while a solid white line beside an HOV lane may be crossed to merge in or out.

teaching.text: The solid white right-edge line is crossed only for an emergency or road hazard, while the solid white line beside an HOV lane may be crossed to merge. Remember: emergency only versus merging.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The solid white right-edge line is crossed only for an emergency or a road hazard, while a solid white line beside an HOV lane may be crossed to merge in or out.

question.text: What do yellow lane lines divide?

answer.text: Yellow lane lines divide lanes of traffic heading in opposite directions.

teaching.text: Yellow lane lines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions. Remember: yellow: opposite directions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Yellow lane lines divide lanes of traffic heading in opposite directions.

question.text: How do white lane lines differ from yellow lane lines?

answer.text: White lane lines divide traffic going the same way, while yellow lane lines divide traffic going opposite ways.

teaching.text: White lane lines divide traffic going the same way, while yellow lane lines divide traffic going opposite ways. Remember: same versus opposite.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: White lane lines divide traffic going the same way, while yellow lane lines divide traffic going opposite ways.

question.text: What may a single yellow line mark on divided highways and one-way streets?

answer.text: A single yellow line may mark the left edge of the pavement on divided highways and on one-way streets.

teaching.text: On divided highways and one-way streets, a single yellow line may mark the left edge of the pavement. Remember: left pavement edge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A single yellow line may mark the left edge of the pavement on divided highways and on one-way streets.

question.text: Which edge does a single white line mark, and which a single yellow line?

answer.text: A single white line can mark the right pavement edge, while a single yellow line can mark the left pavement edge on divided highways and one-way streets.

teaching.text: A single white line can mark the right pavement edge, while a single yellow line can mark the left edge on divided highways and one-way streets. Remember: white right, yellow left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A single white line can mark the right pavement edge, while a single yellow line can mark the left pavement edge on divided highways and one-way streets.

question.text: What is a reversible lane?

answer.text: A reversible lane switches its direction of travel depending on the time of day.

teaching.text: A reversible lane changes its direction of travel depending on the time of day. Remember: direction changes by time.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A reversible lane switches its direction of travel depending on the time of day.

question.text: How are reversible lanes usually marked?

answer.text: Reversible lanes are usually marked with double dashed yellow lines.

teaching.text: Reversible lanes are usually marked with double dashed yellow lines on each side. Remember: double dashed yellow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reversible lanes are usually marked with double dashed yellow lines.

question.text: How can you tell which reversible lanes you may use?

answer.text: Signs beside the road or overhead may tell you which reversible lanes you are allowed to use at that time.

teaching.text: Signs beside the road or overhead may tell you which reversible lanes are open to you at that time. Remember: read the lane signs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Signs beside the road or overhead may tell you which reversible lanes you are allowed to use at that time.

question.text: What do double dashed yellow lines usually signal?

answer.text: Double dashed yellow lines usually signal a reversible lane, whose direction depends on the time of day.

teaching.text: Double dashed yellow lines usually signal a reversible lane, whose direction depends on the time of day. Remember: a reversible lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Double dashed yellow lines usually signal a reversible lane, whose direction depends on the time of day.

question.text: Where do turning rules apply?

answer.text: Turning rules apply everywhere you turn, including driveways and alleys, not just at intersections.

teaching.text: The rules for turning apply wherever you turn, including driveways and alleys as well as intersections. Remember: every turn, everywhere.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turning rules apply everywhere you turn, including driveways and alleys, not just at intersections.

question.text: What three steps make up any turn?

answer.text: To make any turn, signal, slow down and turn smoothly once it is safe.

teaching.text: For any turn, signal, slow down, and make the turn smoothly once it is safe. Remember: signal, slow, turn smoothly.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To make any turn, signal, slow down and turn smoothly once it is safe.

question.text: What should you check for while you turn?

answer.text: While you turn, check for pedestrians, mopeds and bicycles.

teaching.text: As you turn, look out for pedestrians, mopeds and bicycles in your path. Remember: walkers, mopeds, bikes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: While you turn, check for pedestrians, mopeds and bicycles.

question.text: How do you know which lanes to use where turns are allowed from more than one lane?

answer.text: Where turns may be made from more than one lane, signs and pavement markings will show you which lanes to use.

teaching.text: Where turns may be made from more than one lane, signs and pavement markings show which lanes to use. Remember: signs and markings show.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Where turns may be made from more than one lane, signs and pavement markings will show you which lanes to use.

question.text: Are turns allowed at every location?

answer.text: At some locations, signs prohibit turning.

teaching.text: At some locations, signs prohibit turning, so check for them before you turn. Remember: signs may prohibit turns.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At some locations, signs prohibit turning.

question.text: How should you position the car before a right turn?

answer.text: Before a right turn, keep close to the right curb or road edge and do not swing wide before or during the turn.

teaching.text: Before a right turn, stay close to the right curb or edge and do not swing wide before or during the turn. Remember: hug the right, no swinging.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before a right turn, keep close to the right curb or road edge and do not swing wide before or during the turn.

question.text: What must you do before turning right at a red light?

answer.text: To turn right at a red light, you must first come to a complete stop before the marked or unmarked crosswalk.

teaching.text: To turn right on a red light, first come to a complete stop before the marked or unmarked crosswalk. Remember: full stop before crosswalk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To turn right at a red light, you must first come to a complete stop before the marked or unmarked crosswalk.

question.text: What sign should you look for before turning right on red?

answer.text: Look for No Turn On Red signs before you turn right at a red light.

teaching.text: Before turning right at a red light, look for No Turn On Red signs that forbid it. Remember: No Turn On Red.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Look for No Turn On Red signs before you turn right at a red light.

question.text: Whom must you yield to when turning right on red?

answer.text: When turning right on red, always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and oncoming traffic.

teaching.text: When you turn right on red, always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and oncoming traffic. Remember: walkers, bikes, oncoming cars.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When turning right on red, always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and oncoming traffic.

question.text: In which lane should a right turn normally end?

answer.text: Unless signs direct you otherwise, finish a right turn in the right lane of the road you enter.

teaching.text: Unless signs tell you otherwise, finish a right turn in the right lane of the road you enter. Remember: finish in the right lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Unless signs direct you otherwise, finish a right turn in the right lane of the road you enter.

question.text: Where do you approach and begin a left turn on a two-way road?

answer.text: For a left turn on a two-way road, approach in the lane just to the right of the center line and begin the turn just left of the center point of the intersection.

teaching.text: On a two-way road, approach a left turn in the lane just right of the center line and start turning just left of the intersection's center point. Remember: just right of center.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a left turn on a two-way road, approach in the lane just to the right of the center line and begin the turn just left of the center point of the intersection.

question.text: Which lane should you be in after a left turn on a two-way road?

answer.text: When a left turn on a two-way road is complete, you should be in the lane just to the right of the center line, which avoids conflict with other turning traffic.

teaching.text: After a left turn on a two-way road, you should end up in the lane just right of the center line, avoiding other turning traffic. Remember: end just right of center.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a left turn on a two-way road is complete, you should be in the lane just to the right of the center line, which avoids conflict with other turning traffic.

question.text: When a left-turn lane is signed or marked, where must you turn from?

answer.text: When a left-turn lane has been signed or marked, turn left only from that lane and never from any other lane.

teaching.text: When a left-turn lane is signed or marked, make your left turn only from that lane. Remember: use the marked lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a left-turn lane has been signed or marked, turn left only from that lane and never from any other lane.

question.text: How does a marked left-turn lane differ from multi-lane turns?

answer.text: A marked left-turn lane must be used for a left turn, while turns from more than one lane are allowed only where signs and markings show it.

teaching.text: A marked left-turn lane must be used for the turn, while turns from more than one lane are allowed only where signs and markings show it. Remember: marked lane versus signed lanes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A marked left-turn lane must be used for a left turn, while turns from more than one lane are allowed only where signs and markings show it.

question.text: How do you turn left from a one-way road onto another one-way road?

answer.text: For a left turn from a one-way road onto another one-way road, approach in the lane nearest the left curb and turn into the far left lane without swinging wide.

teaching.text: From one one-way road onto another, approach in the lane nearest the left curb and turn into the far left lane without swinging wide. Remember: left curb lane to far left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a left turn from a one-way road onto another one-way road, approach in the lane nearest the left curb and turn into the far left lane without swinging wide.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: left curb lane to far left

question.text: Which left turn may be made against a red light?

answer.text: Turning left from a one-way road onto another one-way road is the only left turn you may make against a red light, after stopping and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless signs prohibit it.

teaching.text: Left from a one-way road onto another one-way road is the only left turn allowed on red, after stopping and yielding, unless signs prohibit it. Remember: one-way to one-way only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turning left from a one-way road onto another one-way road is the only left turn you may make against a red light, after stopping and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless signs prohibit it.

question.text: How does turning right on red differ from turning left on red?

answer.text: Turning right on red needs a full stop before the crosswalk, while turning left on red is allowed only from a one-way road onto another one-way road.

teaching.text: Right on red needs a full stop before the crosswalk, while left on red is allowed only from one one-way road onto another. Remember: right after a stop; left rarely.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turning right on red needs a full stop before the crosswalk, while turning left on red is allowed only from a one-way road onto another one-way road.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: right after a stop; left rarely

question.text: How do you turn left from a two-way road onto a one-way road?

answer.text: For a left turn from a two-way road onto a one-way road, approach in the lane just to the right of the center line and turn into the far left lane of the road you enter.

teaching.text: From a two-way road onto a one-way road, approach just right of the center line and turn into the far left lane. Remember: right of center to far left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a left turn from a two-way road onto a one-way road, approach in the lane just to the right of the center line and turn into the far left lane of the road you enter.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: right of center to far left

question.text: Where do you approach a left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road?

answer.text: For a left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road, approach the intersection in the lane closest to the left curb.

teaching.text: From a one-way road onto a two-way road, approach the intersection in the lane closest to the left curb. Remember: lane nearest left curb.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For a left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road, approach the intersection in the lane closest to the left curb.

question.text: Where does a left turn start from a two-way road versus a one-way road?

answer.text: A left turn from a two-way road starts in the lane just right of the center line, while a left turn from a one-way road starts in the lane nearest the left curb.

teaching.text: A left turn from a two-way road starts just right of the center line, while one from a one-way road starts in the lane nearest the left curb. Remember: center line versus left curb.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A left turn from a two-way road starts in the lane just right of the center line, while a left turn from a one-way road starts in the lane nearest the left curb.

question.text: Where do a right turn and a left turn onto a one-way road end?

answer.text: A right turn normally ends in the right lane of the new road, while a left turn onto a one-way road ends in its far left lane.

teaching.text: A right turn normally ends in the right lane of the new road, while a left turn onto a one-way road ends in its far left lane. Remember: right lane versus far left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A right turn normally ends in the right lane of the new road, while a left turn onto a one-way road ends in its far left lane.

hooks_spoken: White curbs are for passengers, yellow for loading while you stay with the car, and red for no stopping; on a long one-way trip the center lane is usually best.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of painted curbs and one-way streets. White curbs are for passengers, yellow for loading while you stay with the car, and red for no stopping; on a long one-way trip the center lane is usually best. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Cross a broken white line after signaling, cross the edge line only for emergencies or hazards, and never cross a double solid white line.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of white lane lines. Cross a broken white line after signaling, cross the edge line only for emergencies or hazards, and never cross a double solid white line. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Yellow lines divide opposite directions, and double dashed yellow lines usually mark a reversible lane whose direction changes by time.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of yellow lines and reversible lanes. Yellow lines divide opposite directions, and double dashed yellow lines usually mark a reversible lane whose direction changes by time. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Signal, slow and turn smoothly, watch for walkers and bikes, and turn right on red only after a full stop where no sign forbids it.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of turning basics and right turns. Signal, slow and turn smoothly, watch for walkers and bikes, and turn right on red only after a full stop where no sign forbids it. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Left turns start just right of the center line on two-way roads and nearest the left curb on one-way roads, and only one-way to one-way may be made on red.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of left turns. Left turns start just right of the center line on two-way roads and nearest the left curb on one-way roads, and only one-way to one-way may be made on red. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.
